scope: Read-only visual review of 23 saved Chromium forced-color screenshots and their raw axe results. No app, browser, network or Docker run.
sourcePinMethod: The CI owner supplied the saved image provenance. The Chromium report has buildId null. Source excerpts were read directly from this Git commit.
finalExactCi: Pending. This review does not clear the release candidate.

axe.interpretation: The checker retains but excludes forced-mode color-contrast violations from failures. Axe compares authored colors against white here. The exclusions are not a visual pass. Incomplete results are undetermined checks. The visual review found separate control visibility and selected-state defects.

findings.status: confirmed in saved screenshot; correction pending
findings.title: Muted volume controls remain faint
findings.observation: The 70% value is pale gray and the muted slider is faint against the white background. The mute icon remains visible.
findings.cause: The muted state applies opacity: 0.42 to both elements.
findings.recommendedCheck: Use opacity 1 in forced colors and retain the separate mute state cue. Recheck the actual muted and unmuted controls.

findings.status: confirmed in saved screenshot; correction pending
findings.title: Selected party checkmarks remain pale green
findings.observation: The selected cards contain pale green marks inside black boxes. The unchecked Classic Trivia card has an empty box. The faint mark is the main selection difference.
findings.cause: A CSS background image contains the fixed SVG stroke #a4e3b7.
findings.recommendedCheck: Use a system-color mark in forced colors. Keep a visible mark for selected cards and an empty box for unselected cards. Recheck both states.

findings.status: confirmed in saved screenshot; correction pending
findings.title: Shop section selection is visually lost
findings.observation: Basics and Upgrades have the same black text and bottom border. The active section cannot be identified from these controls.
findings.cause: The selected state changes authored border, text and background colors. The unselected transparent border also paints black in the saved forced-color output.
findings.recommendedCheck: Give pressed and unpressed tabs distinct system-color states and a non-color selected cue. Recheck both tabs after selection.

findings.status: confirmed in saved screenshot; correction pending
findings.title: Calibration filter selection is visually lost
findings.observation: All questions is the default selected filter, but its text, border and background look the same as the other four filter buttons.
findings.cause: The selected state changes authored border, background and text colors only.
findings.recommendedCheck: Give the pressed filter a visible system-color state and a non-color selected cue. Recheck each selected filter.

limits: No contrast ratio was measured from painted pixels. Authored-color axe ratios do not establish the ratio of the forced-color screenshot.
One Chromium engine, one emulated forced-color palette and one 1280 by 900 viewport were reviewed. This is not a physical Windows high-contrast test.

Screenshots establish only the saved states. They do not establish keyboard behavior, focus visibility across all controls, hover, answer selection, correct and incorrect results, or successful audio playback.
The calibration screenshot was reviewed as a whole and at native size in top, middle and bottom crops. Every table row was not individually read.
The source report does not include a forced-mode keyboard focus paint result.
Decorative logos and some icons become blank or pale. Visible text still names these elements. This review does not certify every image or every color palette.

representativeCrop.operation: Unscaled crop for native-size visual inspection; the source image was not changed.

references.title: W3C CSS Color Adjustment Module Level 1, section 3.1
supports: System colors are preserved rather than replaced with another forced color.
Background images that contain a URL function are retained.
Opacity is not among the specified forced-color overrides. The need to reset the app muted opacity is an inference from those rules and the saved screenshot.
